messages:
Priya (PM): quick thread — we have a recurring customer ask: full admin console controls for routing & quotas. they want a neat UI. engineering prefers ship-as-api-first. need to pick ordering and criteria.
Sam (Eng): +1 on api-first. lower dev friction for integrators and easier to test. console always balloons scope.
Maya (Product Ops): customers keep bringing it up in onboarding calls; conversion drops when they can't find per-route quotas.
Jorge (Sales): to add — 3 enterprise prospects said console controls are gating renewal. one-off config changes vs programmatic not enough for them.
Alex (SRE): from infra side, console surface adds more attack surface and long-term maintenance. prefer thin admin that calls APIs we already own.
Priya (PM): proposal: evaluate with a small RICE-style score. impact = customer retention (high), reach = 15 enterprise accounts, confidence = 60%, effort = 4 sprints. can someone do a back-of-envelope RICE?
Sam (Eng): rough: Reach=15 -> scale factor 0.4, Impact=7, Confidence=0.6, Effort=4 -> RICE = (0.4*7*0.6)/4 ≈ 0.42.
Maya (Product Ops): compared to shipping API-only with a reference UI (docs + script) — reach might be bigger because self-serve customers adopt faster. Effort maybe 2 sprints.
Jorge (Sales): if we do API-first + a polished admin template for enterprise, we can close the deals and keep engineering velocity.
Priya (PM): alternative sequencing idea: 1) API endpoints (quota, routing, policies) + SDKs + example admin UI (template) 2) measure 30d retention and support tickets 3) decide on investing in managed console. launch criteria: endpoints stable, integration tests, docs + example app, one customer can use end-to-end.
Alex (SRE): add SLOs: API < 100ms p95 for config reads, write durability and audit logs enabled. ops checklist before customer-onboarding.
Sam (Eng): implementation note: we can gate console features behind a feature flag per-org and use the same backend handlers. reduces parallel work.
Maya (Product Ops): UX-minimum for the template: list routes, set quota, simple policy toggle. nothing more. keep it intentionally skinny.
Priya (PM): risk log: a) we under-index on enterprise UX and lose deals, b) we overbuild console and slow core infra. mitigation: ship template + sales pilot.
Jorge (Sales): can we promise pilot in 6 weeks? need demo for one prospect.
Sam (Eng): 6 weeks OK for API + template if we prioritize. requires freezing non-critical work.
Priya (PM): decision: go API-first + example admin template, feature flag for managed console. action items: Sam scope epic + timeline, Alex ops checklist, Maya draft template UX, Jorge pick pilot customer.
Sam (Eng): I'll open the epic and include RICE numbers, acceptance criteria, e2e tests.
Alex (SRE): I'll add deploy runbook + KMS/audit hook to the epic.
Maya (Product Ops): I'll mock Figma screens and a short help doc.
Jorge (Sales): I'll coordinate pilot and send contact to Priya.
DeployBot: sam/deploy requested: create-epic/18923-api-console-template — status: created :white_check_mark:
Priya (PM): thanks all. we'll reconvene in 2 weeks with the epic draft and timeline. :thumbsup:
Maya (Product Ops): noted — will include success metric: pilot conversion + reduction in support tickets within 30 days.
Sam (Eng): adding a note to epic: instrumentation endpoints + metric names for tracking.
Priya (PM): end.
